_note: The de-clutter ruleset: strip every non-informative mark from the chart frame, then format axes/ticks/legends for reading. This is the BBC bbplot 'remove the clutter' philosophy translated into a Vega-Lite config block + per-encoding rules. The Programmer applies _config_block to a chart's "config", then the per-axis rules. The Auditor checks the zero-baseline rule and log-domain rule.
_sources: BBC bbplot R package (the gridline/tick/axis-line/legend de-clutter rules; bbplot is MIT-licensed — these are re-authored as Vega-Lite config). Project component_implementations.json (scale.zero / labelExpr-is-Vega-expr pitfalls this builds on).

_config_block._note: The canonical "config" for an editorial chart, authored for the ALWAYS-ON DARK cinematic stage (the Data2Story page is unconditionally dark; embedChart sets spec.background='transparent', so the chart sits over the dark stage on a dark .chart-card surface). All guide-text + frame ink here is therefore LIGHT BY DEFAULT — this is the CORRECT default, NOT a placeholder to 'restore' to the old light-mode grey (#555/#333/#cbcbcb). MANDATORY light guide text: config.title.color AND config.title.subtitleColor (a SEPARATE property — Vega's subtitle default is DARK and goes INVISIBLE on the dark stage if unset; this was the bug, PIT-62), config.axis.labelColor + titleColor, config.legend.labelColor + titleColor, plus light-on-dark gridColor/domainColor. The Programmer keeps these light over the dark stage (do not swap them back to a dark --muted/--line). SET GUIDE-TEXT COLORS HERE — IN THIS ONE SHARED CONFIG — AND NEVER PER-CHART: every chart must inherit this _config_block (build each chart's "config" from it) so no chart can be missed. Per-chart / 'one chart sets it' is exactly how a guide-text color gets dropped — the WC blog had 10 charts on ONE shared embed() base config that set title.color but OMITTED subtitleColor, so EVERY subtitle was dark-on-dark, yet validate.py Section 17 PASSED because §17 only checks whether `subtitleColor` appears ANYWHERE on the page and one OTHER chart had it locally. The fix is structural: complete THIS shared block (all six guide-text colors light, below), do not patch individual charts. These FRAME/guide inks are NOT data-encoding colors and do NOT redefine design_tokens.json data_color_scales; data-encoding color (sequential/diverging/categorical + the --accent highlight) is owned by design_tokens.json data_color_scales (and encoding_craft.json for CVD-safety), never here.

view._: remove the default chart border box

title._: DARK-STAGE GUIDE TEXT (PIT-62): force a LIGHT title AND subtitle. subtitleColor is a SEPARATE Vega property from color — setting only color leaves the subtitle at Vega's DARK default, which is invisible on the always-on dark cinematic background. Both required.

axisY._: keep ONLY faint major Y gridlines (light-on-dark ~rgba(255,255,255,.18) for the dark stage); drop the Y axis line + Y ticks

axisX._: category/time X: NO X gridlines; keep a thin light-on-dark baseline (domain ~rgba(255,255,255,.45)) for bars/columns; drop X ticks

axis._: LIGHT axis ink (#e8e8e8) for the dark stage — not the old dark #555

legend._: legend on TOP, no legend title (the categories speak for themselves) — or drop the legend entirely and label directly (annotation_layers.json line_end_label). LIGHT legend ink (#e8e8e8) for the dark stage so legend text is not dark-on-dark (PIT-62).

gridlines.rule: Minor gridlines: OFF always. Major gridlines: keep ONLY on the quantitative (value) axis, light (~#cbcbcb), thin. The category axis gets NO gridlines.
gridlines.vega_lite: axisY.grid:true + a faint light-on-dark gridColor (rgba(255,255,255,.18) for the always-on dark stage); axisX.grid:false (for vertical category charts). For horizontal bars, swap: gridlines on the X (value) axis, none on the Y (category) axis.
gridlines.why: Gridlines are scaffolding for reading values; one set, faint, is enough. Two sets of heavy gridlines = a cage.

axis_lines_ticks_titles.rule: Drop axis DOMAIN lines and TICKS where the labels already locate the data (almost always on the value axis). Keep a thin baseline (domain) on the category axis of a bar/column chart (it anchors the zero line). DROP an axis TITLE when it is self-evident or stated in the chart's own title/subtitle (e.g. years on the x-axis need no 'Year' title).
axis_lines_ticks_titles.vega_lite: axis: {domain:false, ticks:false} per axis; title:null on an axis to drop its title; encoding-level "axis":{"title":null} overrides per field.
axis_lines_ticks_titles.why: Every removed line is less ink between the reader and the data (the bbplot principle). Keep only what carries information.

legend.rule: Legend on TOP, horizontal, NO title. Better still: for lines/areas with few series, delete the legend and label series directly at the line end (annotation_layers.json). For a sequential color (choropleth/heatmap) keep a legend WITH units.
legend.vega_lite: config.legend:{orient:'top', title:null}; or encoding-level "legend":null to remove; gradient legend for continuous color keeps title (the units).
legend.why: A top legend reads before the chart; a direct label removes the color->name round-trip entirely.

tick_formatting.rule: Format tick labels for humans: currency ($), percent (%), and abbreviated thousands/millions (12k, 3.4M). Put the UNIT in the axis/chart title, not on every tick, when possible.
tick_formatting.vega_lite_format: Use the encoding's "format" with d3-format strings: "$,.0f" (currency), ".0%" (percent — note Vega multiplies by 100 for %), "~s" (SI abbreviation: 12k, 3.4M), ",.0f" (thousands separator).
tick_formatting.vega_lite_labelExpr: For custom labels use axis.labelExpr — but it is a VEGA EXPRESSION, NOT JavaScript (component_implementations.json). Use Vega helpers: format(datum.value, '$,.0f'), not datum.value.toFixed(). Example abbreviate: "format(datum.value, '~s')". Do NOT call JS methods (.toLocaleString(), template literals) inside labelExpr.
tick_formatting.units_in_title: State units once in the axis/chart title ('Revenue ($m)', 'Share (%)') instead of repeating on each tick.
tick_formatting.anti_pattern: Raw 1200000 on ticks; '%' suffix typed manually while ALSO using a count field (double scaling); .toFixed()/.toLocaleString() inside labelExpr (Vega can't run JS — it silently fails or errors).

zero_baseline_rule.rule: BARS, COLUMNS, and filled AREAS MUST start at zero — their length/area encodes magnitude, so a truncated baseline lies about ratios. LINES, dot plots, and scatter MAY truncate the axis (scale.zero=false) — they encode change/position, not magnitude-from-zero, so zooming in to show variation is honest.

vega_lite.bars_keep_zero: Do NOT set scale.zero=false on a bar/column/area-magnitude y. Leave the default (zero included). If a transform clips it, force "scale":{"zero":true}.
vega_lite.lines_may_truncate: On a line/scatter y where the variation is small relative to the level, set "scale":{"zero":false} PLUS an explicit "domain":[min,max] so the truncation is deliberate, not accidental (component_implementations.json).

zero_baseline_rule.why: Truncating a bar exaggerates differences (the classic misleading chart). Truncating a line is normal practice and shows the signal. The Auditor flags any truncated bar/area baseline.
zero_baseline_rule.anti_pattern: A bar chart with scale.zero=false (overstates differences); a line forced to zero when the action is in a narrow high band (flattens the signal).

point_overflow_rule.rule: Point/scatter/dot marks must not escape the plotting frame. A datum beyond an explicit scale.domain draws OUTSIDE the plot area (over the axis, the chart-card edge, or the bare background). Two-part fix: (1) give scale.domain HEADROOM to the data max/min (pad the domain past the extremes) OR omit domain so Vega auto-fits the extent; AND (2) set "clip": true on the point/scatter mark so nothing renders outside the frame even if a domain is tight. clip is the belt; domain headroom is the suspenders.
point_overflow_rule.vega_lite: mark:{type:'point', clip:true}; and either drop scale.domain (auto-fit) or set domain:[min - pad, max + pad]. Both together: clip:true guarantees no draw outside the frame; the domain headroom keeps the real data inside it.
point_overflow_rule.why: Bars/areas are bounded by the baseline, but points are positioned freely, so any datum past a tight/wrong explicit domain renders over the axis/outside the card. This is the INNER-plot overflow (mark beyond domain) — distinct from the OUTER-SVG overflow (axis/legend overhead wider than spec.width, fixed by fit_and_legibility.svg_must_fit / PIT-03).
point_overflow_rule.detect: Auditor render/vision lens sees points outside the plot or over the card edge — the real catch, since whether a point overflows depends on the DATA vs the domain, which a static check cannot evaluate without running the chart. Static smell only: a point/scatter spec with an explicit scale.domain and NO clip:true on the mark (PIT-65 — soft, no validate.py gate).
point_overflow_rule.anti_pattern: A scatter with an explicit scale.domain that ends at the visible-range max while real data exceeds it, mark un-clipped -> dots draw over the axis / outside the card.

log_scale_rule.rule: Use a log scale when values span orders of magnitude (e.g. 10 to 10,000,000). A log scale requires a strictly POSITIVE domain — log is undefined at 0 and negatives. Never combine a log scale with the zero-baseline rule (they're incompatible).
log_scale_rule.vega_lite: "scale":{"type":"log"} with "domain":[min>0, max]. Filter or floor any zero/negative values first. Label ticks at powers (1, 10, 100, ...) and tell the reader it's log (subtitle/axis title) — readers misread log axes as linear.
log_scale_rule.anti_pattern: A log scale on data containing 0/negatives (renders broken/empty); an unlabeled log axis the reader assumes is linear.

checklist: Guide text LIGHT for the dark stage: config.title.color + config.title.subtitleColor (both — subtitleColor is separate) + config.axis.labelColor/titleColor + config.legend.labelColor/titleColor set light (the dark cinematic background is always on; default Vega guide ink is dark and goes invisible — PIT-62).
Minor gridlines off; one faint set of major gridlines on the value axis only.
Axis domain lines + ticks removed where labels suffice; thin baseline kept on a bar category axis.
Self-evident axis titles dropped; units stated once in the title.
Legend on top with no title — or deleted in favor of direct end-labels.
Ticks formatted ($/%/~s) via format/labelExpr (Vega-expr, NOT JS).
Bars/areas start at zero; lines/scatter may truncate via scale.zero=false + explicit domain.
Any log scale has a strictly positive domain and is labeled as log.
